messages:
emily_s: Heads-up — we just got a DSAR from an EU customer asking for a full account export and deletion. They specifically asked for chats + embeddings. Also mentioned potential legal hold from their counsel. Can we triage impact on KMS/backups and retention-exception process?
raj_k: Thanks. Is this a production tenant on Dedicated or Hosted? Need to know where keys live.
emily_s: Hosted. Model infra uses our eu-west KMS key (arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456:key/abcd). Snapshots are in s3-us-east for backups (cross-region).
sara_legal: If counsel asks for a preservation hold we cannot delete. We need to confirm whether a legal hold is actually required — I can follow up with the requester. Meanwhile treat as potential hold.
ajax_ops: @emily_s do we have an index of which embeddings stores reference that tenant id? I can run a query to list vectors and attached snapshot IDs.
emily_s: There's an internal helper: /ops/tools/emb-indexer — run with tenant id. But careful: don't run any bulk delete until legal confirms.
jordan_sec: Two quick concerns: 1) RBAC — legal needs read-only access to audit logs & keystore access proofs; 2) KMS: if we have to rotate or revoke, how will that affect ability to produce export for DSAR?
raj_k: For hosted, we encrypt embeddings at rest with envelope keys. Customer data encrypted under tenant-specific DEKs wrapped by the eu KMS key. Rotation keeps old ciphertext decryptable unless we explicitly schedule re-encrypt or retire keys.
sara_legal: So we can still produce export even if we rotate, as long as the key isn't scheduled for deletion, correct?
raj_k: Correct. If we revoke/grant access incorrectly it could break access. Don't schedule key deletion.
emily_s: Ops, can you check if any snapshots for tenant are in the 'glacier' tier or have lifecycle pending that would complicate deletion? We want to know propagation timeline.
alex_ops: Running quick check... (results pasted)
```
# ops output
tenant: cust-eu-231
snapshots: 2024-10-12-prod-snap-001 (s3, standard)
old_snap: 2023-11-02-archived (s3, glacier, restore in progress? false)
emb_store: eu-embeddings-prod (replicated to us-east)
object-lock: none
```
alex_ops: Looks like one archived snapshot in glacier but not restored. That could delay a full erase if we need to remove archived copies.
jordan_sec: Ok. Proposal: 1) Put formal hold flag in case counsel confirms — mark tenant as "investigation/hold" to block automatic retention purges and prevent background scrubbing; 2) Create a temporary RBAC grant for sara_legal to view audit trails + evidence; log the grant and timeboxed it; 3) Do not touch KMS keys; ensure no key deletion or rewrap until DSAR closed.
emily_s: Agreed. How do we do timebound RBAC? Can we use short-lived role via identity service?
raj_k: We can create a service role with assume-role for 12 hours and require MFA. I'll prepare a policy: allow logs:Read, kms:DescribeKey (no decrypt), s3:GetObject for exports bucket. If legal needs decrypt proof, we can add kms:Decrypt scoped to specific artifacts and require a two-person approval.
sara_legal: Two-person approval sounds good — need audit trail showing who approved. Also we might need evidence for regulators showing we attempted deletion but preserved for legal hold — audit logs required.
emily_s: Who owns the evidence export? I can coordinate with Raj/Alex. Also we should capture any vuln triage overlap: the DSAR mentions a potential security issue they reported in the same ticket. We must ensure not to leak internal discussion to the requester during export.
jordan_sec: Good point. For the export we should filter internal incident notes and security attachments. Export pipeline should include only customer-facing content. I'll open a small filter rule: exclude channels labeled #internal-investigations and attachments tagged "internal".
alex_ops: I'll run the emb-indexer with dry-run to list objects that would be included: `./emb-indexer --tenant cust-eu-231 --dry-run --output list.txt`
emily_s: Post results to the legal evidence channel (private). Also tag dsar-bot so workflow records the state.
dsar-bot: DSAR intake recorded: id DSAR-2024-482. Status: intake_pending. Assigned to sara_legal. Logs auto-created.
raj_k: Action items I'm taking: 1) prepare short-lived role and policy document; 2) run decrypt smoke on a non-production copy to confirm rotation doesn't break exports; 3) flag KMS key with "no delete" metadata.
emily_s: Action items for ops: verify archived snapshot restore timeline, list cross-region copies, and create a retention-exception request if we need to preserve snapshots beyond normal TTL.
alex_ops: Will do. ETA ~2h for listing, 6-12h if restore needed.
sara_legal: I'll ask counsel whether hold required. If no hold, we proceed with deletion per GDPR timelines after verifying backups and revocation windows. If hold yes, we'll need retention-exception ticket and evidence capture.
jordan_sec: Also, escalate to vuln triage: if the DSAR includes a vuln claim, do not include internal remediation notes in the export. Security to redline exports.
emily_s: Noted. I'll coordinate redaction checklist. Anything else?
raj_k: One more: audit logging. Ensure we snapshot audit logs off-host to immutable store for chain-of-custody and include a signed log excerpt in the evidence package.
sara_legal: Perfect. Thanks everyone. I'll update DSAR-2024-482 and tell requester we acknowledged within 72 hours. :thumbsup:
emily_s: Thanks — I'll follow up once ops/infra reports back.
alex_ops: Posting raw listing to private channel now.
raj_k: I'll paste the brief policy doc here in 1h.
emily_s: Closing thread for now; reopening if new findings. :lock:
